user-insights.outcome: Segments, cohorts and funnels from your event data, with every metric defined.
user-insights.useWhen: Use when product, event, billing or interview data has to inform a product decision.
user-insights.skipWhen: Skip it if you want personas from snapshot columns or proof of cause; observational results stay non-causal.
user-insights.why: Your app already knows what users want. It's in the events, the feedback and the requests. Read it together and you know what to build next, with the numbers to back it.
user-insights.outputContract:
Distinguish two states:

- **Executed analysis:** evidence ledger, metric definitions, data-quality findings, results with denominators/uncertainty, limitations, and decisions.
- **Query plan:** schema mapping, executable queries, expected columns, validation queries, and interpretation rules, with no invented results.

For either state, include justified segments/cohorts only, privacy notes, alternative explanations, recommended action, and how to test it.
checks: Queries use real schema fields and correct grain
Cohort denominators and maturity are correct
PII is minimized and access assumptions are explicit
Observational results are never presented as causal

product-teardown.outcome: A findings table on a product's copy, onboarding and pricing, each tied to evidence.
product-teardown.useWhen: Use when you want to learn from another product's positioning, copy, UX, onboarding, pricing or trust signals.
product-teardown.skipWhen: Skip it if you want to copy a product's words or assets, or guess its revenue from screenshots.
product-teardown.why: Every good product is a pile of decisions you can learn from. Study how one handles copy, onboarding and pricing, and walk away with moves that fit your own product.
checks: Capture date, viewport, and access boundary are stated
Every important claim ties to visible or sourced evidence
Unseen pricing and onboarding are marked unknown, not inferred
Findings state impact, confidence, and limitations

decision-doc.outcome: A decision record with options, tradeoffs, an owner, a first action and a review date.
decision-doc.useWhen: Use when a person or team must choose between approaches or record a choice already made.
decision-doc.skipWhen: Skip it when the choice is settled and you need the build plan; product-spec turns a decision into scope.
decision-doc.why: Most stalled projects are a decision nobody wrote down. Pick one option, name the owner and what would reopen it, and the team stops arguing it again.
checks: States one executable decision or explicit sequence
Claims are sourced, measured, or labeled as assumptions
Reversibility, cost, and downside are explicit
Dissent and the strongest counterargument are represented fairly

product-spec.outcome: A buildable spec: scope, flows, data, permissions, slices and acceptance criteria.
product-spec.useWhen: Use when planning a new product or a change before implementation starts.
product-spec.skipWhen: Skip it while the choice between approaches is still open; settle that with decision-doc first.
product-spec.why: Building goes fast when nobody has to guess. Turn the idea into scope, flows, data and acceptance criteria, and you ship the thing you meant.
product-spec.outputContract:
For a brief, return audience/trigger, problem/evidence, promise/mechanism, smallest value path, scope, exclusions, success signals, assumptions, and open questions.

For a buildable or change spec, add flows/states, architecture fit, data and authorization, interfaces, non-functional requirements, rollout/migration, vertical slices, acceptance criteria, verification, risks, and decisions. For an audit, return findings with evidence, impact, and required correction rather than silently rewriting product intent.
checks: Scope traces to a stated user outcome
Facts, assumptions, and open questions are kept distinct
Failure states, data ownership, and authorization are covered
Acceptance criteria are testable

agent-instructions.outcome: Scoped AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or Cursor rules built from what your repo actually runs.
agent-instructions.useWhen: Use when coding-agent guidance is missing, stale, duplicated or conflicting.
agent-instructions.skipWhen: Skip it if you want generic agent advice or a file for every vendor; it writes only what the repo proves, for the runtime you name.
agent-instructions.why: Agents work best when they know how your repo actually runs. Give them the real commands and rules, and they stop guessing and breaking the build.
checks: Every path, script, port, and env variable exists in the repo
Nested files never contradict inherited rules
Unverified syntax is labeled unverified, not presented as established
Documented-only commands are never described as tested

supabase.outcome: Supabase tables with migrations, grants, RLS, typed clients and denied-access tests.
supabase.useWhen: Use when integrating Supabase or repairing data access and tenant isolation.
supabase.skipWhen: Skip it if you are not on Supabase, or want the same four CRUD policies stamped on every table.
supabase.why: Most Supabase bugs are access bugs. Get tables, policies and typed clients right from the start, and every user only ever sees their own data.
supabase.outputContract: Report tables/functions/storage changed, migration files, grants and RLS policies with auth strategy, client/session changes, type-generation command/result, negative authorization tests, and remaining linked-project/dashboard/production steps.
checks: Local migrations reset and apply cleanly
Schema and generated types show no drift
Anonymous, other-user, and other-tenant access is denied
Attempts to change row ownership are tested

auth-implementation.outcome: Sign-in, sessions and an access matrix enforced next to every protected read and write.
auth-implementation.useWhen: Use when adding sign-in, identity sync, account linking, roles or access control.
auth-implementation.skipWhen: Skip it if you want a new identity provider picked for you; it keeps the one you have unless you decide to switch.
auth-implementation.why: Sign-in is the easy part. Making every route check who's asking is the hard part. Get both right and nobody reads data that isn't theirs.
auth-implementation.outputContract: Report provider/version and identity model, files/migrations changed, access matrix and enforcement points, sync strategy, RLS/grants, environment-variable names, automated verification evidence, and manual dashboard/backfill/production checks.
checks: New sign-up, returning login, logout, and expiry are tested
Every protected resource rejects unauthenticated and other-user requests
Cross-tenant and non-admin access is tested and denied
Replayed sync and account linking are tested

interface-design.outcome: A working interface whose tokens, states and layout follow from the product's job.
interface-design.useWhen: Use when creating or redesigning pages, dashboards, workflows or components.
interface-design.skipWhen: Skip it when only the words are wrong (ui-copy) or a finished page only breaks on phones (mobile-first).
interface-design.why: A good screen comes from the product's job, not a template. Design from the real content and every state, and people find what they came for.
checks: Renders checked at desktop and narrow mobile widths
Keyboard navigation, visible focus, and touch targets work
Contrast, reduced motion, and zoom behavior are checked
Placeholders and invented claims are removed

ui-copy.outcome: Interface copy for every state, written against what the product actually does.
ui-copy.useWhen: Use when buttons, forms, errors, empty states or notifications must match system behavior and voice.
ui-copy.skipWhen: Skip it for marketing pages (landing-copy) or to force a casual, lowercase voice onto the product.
ui-copy.why: Interface words are part of the product. Write them from what the code actually does, and users know what happens before they click.
ui-copy.outputContract:
### Audit

Deliver manifest coverage, prioritized findings, exact source locations, before/after repairs grounded in behavior, decisions to preserve, and states or channels that could not be inspected.

### Generate or flow rewrite

Organize copy by flow and state rather than a fixed list of fields:

```text
[Flow / screen / state]
Purpose and system behavior:
Visible copy:
Actions and destinations:
Accessible names or announcements:
Variables and localization notes:
Source/content owner:
```

### Implement

Update the correct source of truth, preserve unrelated strings, and report files changed, migrations or message-ID changes, rendered states checked, and unverified channels.
checks: Every consequential line matches the actual action and state
Failure and destructive flows exercised in the running product
Plurals, interpolation, and long translations are tested
No placeholder copy or fictional proof reaches production

ai-product-development.outcome: An AI feature with a typed server contract, every UI state, evals and cost controls.
ai-product-development.useWhen: Use when building AI into an app or auditing an AI feature before it ships.
ai-product-development.skipWhen: Skip it for a repo-wide AI cost and margin audit; ai-cost-audit owns that.
ai-product-development.why: An AI feature is a product, not a prompt. Typed contracts, every UI state, evals and cost limits mean it holds up when real users hit it.
ai-product-development.outputContract: Report the chosen interaction and why, server/UI paths changed, state coverage, safety and permission boundaries, evaluation results, latency/cost observations, usage-settlement behavior, verification evidence, and remaining provider or production setup.
checks: Mid-stream failure, cancellation, and timeout paths are tested
Tool actions tested against prompt injection and cross-tenant IDs
Execution-time authorization and usage settlement hold under concurrency
Evaluation set runs alongside lint, type, test, and build

payments-with-dodo.outcome: Dodo checkout, subscriptions and verified webhooks driving server-side entitlements.
payments-with-dodo.useWhen: Use when adding Dodo billing or auditing its full lifecycle.
payments-with-dodo.skipWhen: Skip it if you bill through another provider; it will not install Dodo beside one without a migration plan.
payments-with-dodo.why: Billing breaks quietly. Wire checkout, webhooks, entitlements and refunds end to end, and people get exactly what they paid for, every time.
payments-with-dodo.outputContract: Report product/entitlement mapping, SDK and environment detected, files/migrations changed, checkout/portal paths, webhook inbox and state transitions, payload minimization/access/retention decisions, server enforcement points, test evidence/event IDs, and exact dashboard/production steps still required.
checks: Duplicate and concurrent webhooks are tested in test mode
Invalid webhook signatures are tested
Renewal, cancellation, failed payment, and refund flows are tested
Stored subscriptions reconcile against the Dodo API

credit-metering.outcome: Usage credits on an append-only ledger with reserve, capture, release and refund.
credit-metering.useWhen: Use when an app meters consumable usage with credits.
credit-metering.skipWhen: Skip it for plain subscriptions with nothing consumable to meter; payments-with-dodo covers billing itself.
credit-metering.why: Credits are money, so treat them like a ledger. Reserve, capture and refund cleanly, and usage stays fair even with retries and parallel requests.
credit-metering.outputContract: Report the denomination and policies, schema/migrations, ledger operations and invariants, protected usage paths, provider/product mapping, UI reconciliation, verification evidence, and remaining dashboard or production setup.
checks: Reserve, capture, and release flows are tested
Ledger and balance invariants hold under concurrent spend
Payment replay and out-of-order events are tested
Refunds, clawbacks, and promo races are tested

rate-limit.outcome: Upstash limits on Next.js routes with trusted identifiers, 429 headers and outage rules.
rate-limit.useWhen: Use when protecting Next.js routes from abuse or runaway cost.
rate-limit.skipWhen: Skip it if you are not on Upstash Redis, or expect rate limits alone to stop abuse; they are one layer.
rate-limit.why: Every public route is a bill waiting to happen. Limit by who's calling, decide what happens when Redis is down, and abuse stops costing you.
rate-limit.outputContract: Report the policy table, identifier trust model, files/env names changed, outage behavior, response headers, layered controls, automated test evidence, and remaining Upstash/deployment configuration.
checks: Allowed, blocked, and reset behavior tested with a controllable clock
Spoofed forwarding headers are tested
Route isolation and anonymous versus authenticated keys are tested
Store timeout and outage behavior is tested

email-with-resend.outcome: Consent-aware Resend email with queues, suppression, idempotency and signed webhooks.
email-with-resend.useWhen: Use when an app needs transactional, lifecycle or campaign email through Resend.
email-with-resend.skipWhen: Skip it for cold email to people who never signed up; that is cold-outreach.
email-with-resend.why: Email is where trust is won or lost. Send with consent, suppression and retries handled, and the right message lands exactly once.
email-with-resend.outputContract: Report message classes and triggers, files/templates/jobs changed, sender and environment-variable names, consent/preferences/suppression behavior, webhook and idempotency design, verification evidence/message IDs, and remaining DNS/dashboard/production checks.
checks: Returned API errors and thrown network errors are both tested
Webhooks tested with signed, invalid, and replayed payloads
Bounce and complaint suppression is tested
Sends go only to test recipients until production confirmed

remove-ai-slop.outcome: A ranked report of generic design and copy patterns, with exact before and after fixes.
remove-ai-slop.useWhen: Use when an interface looks or reads generic and you want rendered evidence before changing it.
remove-ai-slop.skipWhen: Skip it for prose voice edits (humanize) or to impose a new house style on the interface.
remove-ai-slop.why: Generic design makes a product forgettable. Find the patterns that read as AI-made, see each fix side by side, and your product looks like yours.
remove-ai-slop.outputContract:
Stop before editing. Lead with a prioritized summary ranked by user impact, frequency, confidence, and repair cost. In focused work, report all in-scope findings. In representative or exhaustive work, group repeated source decisions so the report does not duplicate the same repair for every rendered instance. Use these sections when applicable:

```text
COPY MANIFEST COVERAGE
Scope: [surfaces, routes, channels, locales, states]
Unavailable: [anything not inspected]
Unique source decisions: [count]  Rendered instances: [count]
Baseline: [hard bans, unverified claims, convergence clusters]

HARD SLOP — REMOVE
H1. [route, file:line] — [pattern]
    Before: [exact original]
    After: [verified replacement, deletion, or BLOCKED — CONTENT REQUIRED]
    Evidence: [exact code plus rendered evidence]
    Why it fails: [specific diagnosis]
    Verdict: Remove it.

CONTEXTUAL SLOP
C1. [route, file:line] — [pattern, score, HIGH or MEDIUM confidence]
    Verdict: [STRONG PRESUMPTION, CONTEXTUAL SIGNAL, or CANDIDATE]
    Before: [exact original]
    After: [product-specific repair or BLOCKED — CONTENT REQUIRED]
    Evidence: [repetition, mismatch, co-occurrence, render or copy manifest]

COPY CONVERGENCE
CC1. [convergence type and normalized pattern or term, score, confidence]
     Instances: [routes, states, files, and exact excerpts]
     Impact: [how unrelated jobs were flattened or terminology drifted]
     Repair: [which source decisions change and which terminology stays]
     Why it fails: [unrelated jobs forced through one voice or template]

QUALITY DEFECTS
Q1. [route, file:line] — [accessibility, semantics, performance, claim, or state-integrity issue]
    Evidence: [code, behavior, source, or contradiction]
    Impact: [user, trust, task, or compliance consequence]
    Provenance: [verified, unverified, contradicted, or not applicable]
    Recommendation: [repair, provenance request, or blocked status]

DECISIONS TO PRESERVE
P1. [element] — [why it is intentional, specific, and effective]
```

Critique the artifact, not its author. Be direct about objective hard slop: write “This placeholder is exposed as finished copy. Remove it,” not “You may want to consider refining it.” For visual defaults, state the rendered evidence and confidence rather than presenting taste as fact.

For every actionable source decision, show the exact before and after when the replacement can be grounded in repository evidence. When content or product intent is missing, state the required decision instead of generating speculative alternatives. Use real product copy and existing tokens rather than placeholders. Ground rewritten claims in cited repository evidence. Treat `UNVERIFIED` and `BLOCKED — CONTENT REQUIRED` as report-only statuses; never write them into user-facing copy. When rendering is available, compare the same route, viewport, state, data, and animation setting.

Do not use canonical replacements such as flat black, one accent, 8px radii, a two-column list, uniformly terse prose, or default casual voice unless the product evidence supports them. State the intended design or copy job first, then propose the smallest repair that performs it.
checks: Hard-ban pattern counts reach zero, not just renamed
Same routes, viewports, and states re-rendered after edits
No cliché replaced with another cliché
Material claims are sourced, narrowed, marked UNVERIFIED, or removed

mobile-first.outcome: Measured narrow-screen fixes with before and after numbers at 320, 375, 768 and 1440.
mobile-first.useWhen: Use when a page clips, overflows, stacks poorly or fails on touch.
mobile-first.skipWhen: Skip it when the page's structure or message is wrong; fix that with landing-page or interface-design first.
mobile-first.why: Most people meet your product on a phone. Fix what breaks between 320 and 768 pixels, measured before and after, and it works in their hand.
checks: Layouts re-measured at 320, 375, 768, and 1440px
200% zoom and 320px reflow are tested
Touch controls, orientation changes, and text enlargement are exercised
Software keyboard and long localized labels are tested

performance-diagnosis.outcome: A measured baseline, a root cause or ranked hypotheses, and before and after numbers.
performance-diagnosis.useWhen: Use when an app is slow, spikes resources, reload-loops, regresses or fails Web Vitals.
performance-diagnosis.skipWhen: Skip it if you want a quick fix without a reproduction; it measures first and edits only when asked.
performance-diagnosis.why: Slow is a symptom, not a cause. Measure first, find the real bottleneck, and the page gets faster where users actually feel it.
performance-diagnosis.outputContract: Report symptom and reproduction, baseline, evidence, root cause or ranked remaining hypotheses, files changed only if authorized, before/after metrics, correctness checks, confidence level, and next measurement. Do not claim a cause or improvement without observed evidence.
checks: Same reproduction rerun under the same conditions
Median and tail values compared, cold and warm separately
Caching and concurrency changes pass correctness tests
Lab results paired with field data when available

search-ready.outcome: Prioritized SEO, schema and AI-crawler fixes per route, checked against the live site.
search-ready.useWhen: Use when preparing or maintaining a live site for search and answer engines.
search-ready.skipWhen: Skip it if you expect guaranteed rankings or AI citations; it never promises either.
search-ready.why: Good pages go unread when search can't understand them. Fix metadata, schema and crawl rules route by route, and people find you.
checks: Templates and edge states sampled beyond the homepage
Schema matches visible content and passes validation
Redirects, canonicals, robots, and sitemap agree
AI-search recommendations state confidence and avoid guarantees

social-sharing.outcome: Correct canonical URLs, Open Graph tags and preview images for every shared route.
social-sharing.useWhen: Use when shared links show missing, stale, generic, private or wrong previews.
social-sharing.skipWhen: Skip it for indexation, sitemaps and schema; search-ready owns that.
social-sharing.why: A shared link is a first impression. Get the titles, images and previews right on every route, and every share looks intentional.
social-sharing.outputContract:
For each defect, report:

```text
[route family and representative URL]
Source: [file:line or generator]
Resolved value: [observed tag, URL, or image response]
Expected behavior: [route contract]
Impact: [wrong identity, missing preview, stale image, privacy risk, or broken action]
Repair: [specific source change]
Verification: [automated and deployed check]
```

Separate source-code candidates from defects confirmed in rendered HTML or image responses.

For repair or implementation work, also return:

- files and route families changed;
- metadata sources, canonical policy, and image fallback implemented;
- representative or exhaustive coverage manifest, including every enumerated image response in exhaustive mode;
- local and deployed checks with observed status, content type, dimensions, and resolved values;
- cache/debugger state and any refresh still pending;
- routes, dynamic sets, credentials, or production checks that remain unverified.
checks: Resolved HTML has one canonical URL and OG tags
Every preview image returns correct status and dimensions
Dynamic routes never borrow another record's title or image
Public URLs fetched after deploy, not just localhost

readme.outcome: A README checked against the repo, with each command marked as run or documented only.
readme.useWhen: Use when repository documentation is missing, inaccurate or hard to follow.
readme.skipWhen: Skip it if you want badges, banners and GIFs for show; it adds visuals only when they explain something.
readme.why: A README is the front door of a repo. Check that every command actually runs, and new people get from clone to working in minutes.
checks: Every path, port, and env variable matches the repo
Install and minimal usage run in a clean environment
Code blocks and links validated with available tooling
Anything not executed is labeled as such

deploy-check.outcome: A READY, BLOCKED or NEEDS CONFIRMATION verdict with the evidence behind it.
deploy-check.useWhen: Use before deploying, pushing or approving a release.
deploy-check.skipWhen: Skip it if you want it to deploy for you; it never pushes or deploys without separate permission.
deploy-check.why: Most bad deploys were visible before the push. Check tests, secrets, migrations and rollback first, and you ship knowing it's safe.
deploy-check.outputContract: Report release base/head and scope, commands with exit status, blockers, warnings, migrations and rollout order, config/secrets findings without values, external confirmations, rollback/roll-forward notes, and the evidence behind the verdict. Never say “safe to push” solely because type checking passed.
checks: Verdict is READY, BLOCKED, or NEEDS CONFIRMATION with evidence
Every command reported with its exit status
Secrets findings reported without printing values
Never calls a release safe from type checks alone

changelog.outcome: Changelog copy from a verified git range, each item traced to its commits.
changelog.useWhen: Use when preparing weekly updates, release summaries or social changelog cards.
changelog.skipWhen: Skip it to judge whether a release is safe to ship; run deploy-check for that.
changelog.why: Shipping counts for more when people can see it. Turn the git log into notes users understand, and every release earns attention.
changelog.outputContract:
Deliver the requested artifact plus:

```text
Range: [commits/tags/dates and branch]
Audience and channel: [who/where]
Release status: [verified live, released, unreleased, or mixed]
Items: [final count]
Provenance: [item -> commits or paths]
Statistics: [definitions and values, if used]
Artifacts: [paths and dimensions]
Limitations: [deployment or content facts not verified]
```

For a prose-only request, do not create HTML. For an audit request, stop at findings and proposed copy unless the user also asked for edits.
checks: Every claim re-checked against the selected release range
No breaking, security, or migration change is hidden
Statistics recomputed with commands that match their labels
Visual cards rendered at target size for clipping and overflow

skill-creator.outcome: A portable SKILL.md package with routed references, validation and behavioral evals.
skill-creator.useWhen: Use when authoring, improving, merging or validating SKILL.md packages.
skill-creator.skipWhen: Skip it for a one-off prompt; it packages workflows you repeat.
skill-creator.why: Any workflow you repeat is a skill waiting to be written. Package it with tests, and your agent does it the same good way every time.
checks: Directory name and frontmatter name agree
Every relative Markdown link resolves
Repository skill validator passes on every touched package
Behavioral evals rerun after structural changes

landing-copy.outcome: A landing-page copy deck built on one defensible claim and the proof behind it.
landing-copy.useWhen: Use when product, pricing, campaign or waitlist pages need clearer positioning.
landing-copy.skipWhen: Skip it if the page needs proof you don't have; it flags the gap instead of inventing numbers or urgency.
landing-copy.why: Visitors decide in seconds. Lead with one claim you can prove, and they understand why it matters to them before they scroll.
checks: Every material claim maps to product behavior or a source
Major propositions pass a competitor swap test
CTA text, destination, and actual commitment agree
No proof, statistic, urgency, or guarantee is invented

landing-page.outcome: A built or repaired landing page around one visitor, one decision and real proof.
landing-page.useWhen: Use when a marketing page must do one clear job and needs building, repair or an audit.
landing-page.skipWhen: Skip it when only the words are wrong (landing-copy) or only the phone layout breaks (mobile-first).
landing-page.why: A landing page has one job: help one visitor make one decision. Build it around that and real proof, and more of them say yes.
checks: Renders checked at narrow, tablet, desktop, and 200% zoom
Primary action, forms, errors, and keyboard path are exercised
Claims, links, analytics events, and share previews are verified
Reports gaps against the brief instead of declaring success

image-editing.outcome: Edited images that keep product identity, exact text and earlier approved changes.
image-editing.useWhen: Use when a supplied image needs reference-based edits or successive revisions.
image-editing.skipWhen: Skip it if no image-editing tool or API is configured; installing it grants no model access.
image-editing.why: Edited images drift away from the original. Track the references and check every revision, and the product still looks like itself.
image-editing.outputContract: Return the image files, the model identity if exposed, which changes passed inspection, and specific unresolved defects. For a revision chain, identify the chosen base and final output. Do not claim measured fidelity, superiority, or cross-runtime compatibility without an actual recorded test.
checks: Each requested change and preserved detail checked separately
Exact copy checked with OCR and visual inspection
Retries start from the last approved base
Unchecked images are never labeled approved

demo-video.outcome: A Remotion demo with a timed beat sheet, script, captions and rendered files.
demo-video.useWhen: Use when a product or technical claim needs a storyboard or a rendered video.
demo-video.skipWhen: Skip it if you want motion for its own sake; every beat has to show proof of the claim.
demo-video.why: A demo is the fastest way to show what you built. Plan the beats, write the script, render the video, and people get it in a minute.
checks: Every requested deliverable renders with matching resolution and duration
Frames around scene boundaries are deterministic
Narration never claims unavailable product behavior
Captions verified against the final audio

analytics.outcome: An event plan with metric contracts, plus error tracking and health checks wired in.
analytics.useWhen: Use when designing events, consent-aware tracking, error monitoring, health checks or dashboards.
analytics.skipWhen: Skip it for A/B tests and staged rollouts; product-experiments owns assignment and exposure.
analytics.why: You can't improve what you don't measure. Define the events that matter, wire them correctly, and decisions start from real numbers.
checks: Event names and properties confirmed in the provider
Logout reset never merges the wrong people
Test errors are redacted, tagged, and source-mapped
Anything needing production credentials is reported as manual setup

product-launch.outcome: A launch plan with positioning, a few channels, a tested signup path and metrics.
product-launch.useWhen: Use when preparing a product launch or learning from one.
product-launch.skipWhen: Skip it if you want ranking hacks for platform algorithms; it claims no knowledge of opaque rankings.
product-launch.why: A launch is a plan, not a post. Pick the audience, the channels and the signup path, and launch day turns into actual users.
checks: Every public link and conversion path works when deployed
Signup, attribution, and activation events are observed
Platform rules are sourced and date-stamped
Owners, incident path, and rollback are explicit

cold-outreach.outcome: A send-ready cold message or sequence, with facts to confirm kept out of the copy.
cold-outreach.useWhen: Use when contacting prospects, investors, partners or candidates you don't know yet.
cold-outreach.skipWhen: Skip it for email to your own users; email-with-resend handles consent-based product email.
cold-outreach.why: Cold messages work when they're about the reader. Lead with a real reason to talk, keep the facts checkable, and more people reply.
checks: The opener depends on this specific recipient
Every material claim is verified or marked for confirmation
One clear ask or next step per message
Opt-outs, bounces, and replies have stop or routing rules

humanize.outcome: Your draft without generic AI patterns, still in your voice, with the changes listed.
humanize.useWhen: Use when writing sounds synthetic, repetitive, over-polished or unlike its author.
humanize.skipWhen: Skip it when the substance is the problem; landing-copy, cold-outreach, readme or ui-copy fix content.
humanize.why: Readers stop trusting text that sounds generated. Strip the AI patterns, keep the facts and the voice, and it reads like a person wrote it.
humanize.outputContract:
Adapt the output to the size and mode.

For edit mode:

1. Return the complete edited draft without inline commentary.
2. Add a short `What changed` section grouped by material pattern or structural decision.
3. Add `Preserved` when naming deliberate voice choices helps the user trust the edit.
4. Add `Needs you` only for unresolved facts, claims, or voice decisions.

For a one-line or very short edit, return the edit and one sentence of rationale; do not force four empty sections.

For detect mode, list the pattern, exact excerpt, evidence tier, consequence, and repair direction. Also identify specific passages that already work. Do not rewrite unless requested.
checks: The author would recognize the position and voice
Factual meaning and calibrated uncertainty survive the edit
Amount changed matches the evidence
No uniform staccato or corporate polish is introduced

product-experiments.outcome: An experiment with stable assignment, logged exposure and a decision rule set in advance.
product-experiments.useWhen: Use when testing product behavior with flags, exposure tracking, staged releases or A/B tests.
product-experiments.skipWhen: Skip it if you want a ship call from underpowered data; it reports invalid or inconclusive instead.
product-experiments.why: Most tests prove nothing because the rules come after the data. Set the decision rule first, and every result tells you what to do.
checks: Assignment is stable and matches the intended unit
Exposure is deduplicated and joins to outcome events
Kill switch and rollback are tested
Sample-ratio mismatch and event completeness are checked

ai-cost-audit.outcome: Cost per action, user and plan from real usage, with savings ranked by risk.
ai-cost-audit.useWhen: Use when AI cost, margin, pricing, model choice or savings must be measured or verified.
ai-cost-audit.skipWhen: Skip it if you want a cheaper model picked from a price table; it needs eval data and current official prices.
ai-cost-audit.why: AI costs hide inside every call. Price each action, user and plan from real usage, and you see what to cut without hurting quality.
checks: Inventory covers retries, fallbacks, background jobs, and non-text operations
Measured and estimated inputs stay distinguishable
Bottom-up totals reconcile to billed totals when billing exists
Every recommendation has a quality gate and rollback path

fundraising.outcome: A candid raise or no-raise call, a claim-to-evidence map and round math that adds up.
fundraising.useWhen: Use when deciding whether to raise, preparing a raise or improving an active one.
fundraising.skipWhen: Skip it if you want claims without evidence; unsupported traction, logos or investor interest get flagged.
fundraising.why: Investors fund a story the numbers back up. Tie every claim to evidence and get the round math right, and the pitch holds up under questions.
checks: Metric definitions, periods, and denominators stay consistent
Round amount, use of funds, runway, and milestones agree
Investor-fit claims never imply investor interest
Unsupported pitch claims are labeled as hypotheses
